paragraphs.text: DeepSeek Harness plugin: out-of-band progress narration for the Web UI and dsh-tui
# dsh-progress-summary

Out-of-band progress narration for DeepSeek Harness: a cheap auxiliary model turns the live
chain of

thought into one short status line, shown above the composer in the Web UI and on the
dsh-tui statu

t into one short status line, shown above the composer in the Web UI and on the
dsh-tui status line.
## Where it shows

- **Web**: the row above the composer (the input dock), not the transcript's process rows.
- **dsh-t

ui**: the keyed status line above the prompt.
- **Switch**: Settings → General → **Show progress sum

mary**. Turning it off cancels every
auxiliary call and clears the TUI row immediately.
- Other knob
s (model, interval, token floor, language) live on the plugin's page in Plugins.
The transcript's four work-details modes are untouched; this plugin does not add a fifth mode.
## Why out-of-band

Codex-style progress text comes from a model-side channel (`reasoning.summary` plus `commentary`
mes
sages). DeepSeek exposes only raw `reasoning_content`, so there are two ways to approximate it:

- **Prompt nudging** (what the existing working-activity / progress-narrator plugins do): ask the
ma

in model to narrate each step. Cheap, but it competes with the task for output budget, and
OpenAI's

own Codex migration guide recommends removing exactly this kind of preamble prompt.
- **Out-of-band

narration** (this plugin): the main model is untouched; a second, tiny request
reads the recent reas
oning and writes one line.
The cost is an extra call; the benefit is that the task never competes with its own status text.
## Trigger policy
Two layers: **free lines** update at every boundary, **model lines** fire only before a tool call.
| Trigger | Output | Cost |

| Turn start (opt-in) | "Analyzing the request" | 0 |
| Every tool call (opt-in) | a line derived fr

om the tool name and arguments | 0 |
| **Before a tool call**, with both floors met | one sentence f

rom the auxiliary model | 1 call |
| Turn end | idle, clearing both surfaces | 0 |
The model line requires both:

1. **Time**: at least `minIntervalMs` since the last model line (default 20s).
2. **Tokens**: at lea

st `minTokens` of new reasoning since then (default 600; `charsPerToken`
defaults to 3, so roughly 1

f new reasoning since then (default 600; `charsPerToken`
defaults to 3, so roughly 1800 characters).

A tool call is the only trigger that starts a model line because it is the one point where the
prece

ding chain of thought is known to be complete: the model has committed to an action. A pause
in the

stream proves nothing (network jitter, a provider that emits two tokens and stalls, ordinary
tokeniz
ation gaps), which is why there is no timer-based trigger.

Below either floor the material stays buffered and the next tool boundary re-checks. A failed call
r

eturns the consumed characters and retries at the next boundary. Turns without tool calls get no
mod
el line at all — a deliberate trade: rather than cut into a reasoning block, stay quiet.

The two free rows are off by default (`quickLines: false`): the dock is a summary surface, not a
sec

ond command log. The prompt also forbids naming tools, commands, or paths, because the
transcript al
ready shows every call.
Caps: `maxPerTurn` (default 40) calls per turn, 96 output tokens per call, `effort=off`.
## Install
### From a git tag (no registry needed)
[代码示例省略，未执行]

`dsh plugin add` forwards the spec to pnpm, so any pnpm git form works:
`github:user/repo#tag`, `git

+https://github.com/user/repo.git#tag`, or the plain
`https://github.com/user/repo#tag`. The tag pin

s the version; the package has no build step, so
pnpm clones it and installs its dependencies from t

n; the package has no build step, so
pnpm clones it and installs its dependencies from the registry.
### From npm (once published)
[代码示例省略，未执行]

The package declares `dsh.bundle.patch`, so `dsh plugin add` appends it to the profile's bundle
list

; `cordis.patch.yml` inserts the `progress-summary` row and `dsh.client` makes the Web client
load t

he browser half. The plugin deliberately depends on **no DSH core package**: the session
module and

the record-append function come from the Loader's own module instance at runtime, so
installing it c
an never shadow the host's core packages with different versions.
Remove with `dsh plugin --profile web remove dsh-progress-summary`.
### Local development (`link:`)
[代码示例省略，未执行]

`link:` is a development convenience: the profile holds a symlink, so a source edit plus a restart
i
s enough. It has no bearing on publishing.
## Configuration
| Key | Default | Meaning |

| `enabled` | `true` | Master switch; also the Settings toggle (live) |
| `provider` / `model` | `au

to` | `auto` follows the session's own route; otherwise pin a route |
| `effort` | `off` | Reasoning

effort for the auxiliary call |
| `maxTokens` | `96` | Output cap for one line |
| `timeoutMs` | `8

000` | Abort a single call after this long |
| `minIntervalMs` | `20000` | Time floor between two mo

del lines (live) |
| `minTokens` | `600` | Token floor at a tool boundary (live) |
| `charsPerToken`

| `3` | Divisor used for the token estimate |
| `excerptChars` | `700` | Reasoning tail sent to the

model |
| `maxLineChars` | `128` | Hard cap for the rendered line (characters) |
| `maxPerTurn` | `

40` | Hard cap on auxiliary calls per turn (live) |
| `lang` | `auto` | `auto` follows the host loca

le; `zh` / `en` pin it |
| `publish` | `true` | Commit ignorable records so the Web UI receives line

s |
| `tui` | `true` | Contribute the line to a composed TUI |
| `quickLines` | `false` | Opt into t

he free turn-start/per-tool lines |
| `subagents` | `false` | Narrate subagent sessions too |
| `deb
ug` | `true` | Append a bounded diagnostics log under `~/.dsh/` |
Fields marked live are volatile: a save takes effect on the next tool boundary, without a restart.
## Known limitations

- One ignorable record is committed per published line (roughly 10–20 per turn at the defaults);
set

`publish: false` to keep the log clean, at the cost of the Web line.
- Turns with no tool call prod

uce no model line.
- The line is capped at 128 characters and rendered on at most two lines.
- A mis
configured provider/model fails silently; the UI simply has no line.
